Reproducing Neupane, Fiete and Jazayeri (2024) from dandiset 000897¶

Paper. Neupane S, Fiete I, Jazayeri M (2024). Mental navigation in the primate entorhinal cortex. Nature 630, 704-711. doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07557-z. The claims file (claims/000897/10.1038-s41586-024-07557-z.yaml) was written from the version of record in Europe PMC (PMC11224022): main text, Methods and Extended Data legends, with the correction of 4 July 2024, and the paper's code (github.com/jazlab/Neupane_Fiete_Jazayeri_mental_navigation, commit 4bee109).

Dandiset. DANDI:000897, version 0.240605.1710 (doi:10.48324/dandi.000897/0.240605.1710). The paper links the dandiset without a version; this is its only published version, and the draft lists the same 30 files with the same total size. Only the *_behavior+ecephys.nwb file of each session is read (trials, sorted units, eye and joystick traces); the *_ecephys.nwb files hold the raw voltage.

What the dandiset holds. 15 sessions (monkey A 6, monkey M 9) of the paper's 32 (A 17, M 15), with 364 and 729 units against the paper's 614 and 864. Proportions, not counts, can therefore be compared with the paper's.

Methods come from the claims file, and details it lacks from the paper, cited in mnav.py and in each section. The notebook takes about 30 minutes, most of it the PI of every unit, the surrogate nulls, the ANOVAs, streaming the eye and joystick traces and the CAN model.

The dandiset holds 15 sessions (A 6, M 9) of the paper's 32 (A 17, M 15), with 364 units in monkey A and 729 in M, against 614 and 864 in the paper. The monkey A files label units with phy's quality (good, mua, noise, unsorted); 103 of the 364 are labelled noise, which the paper's "single units and multi-units" would not include. The monkey M files carry only Kilosort's KSLabel (good, mua). Units are analysed here as the files hold them, all labels included; the count without noise units is given as a variant where it matters.

The trial table's ta takes the ten values +-0.65 to +-3.25 s, as the six-landmark line with 0.65 s spacing has, and the joystick offset minus onset equals |tp| within about 20 ms, so tp is the produced vector in seconds, signed as ta. In monkey A ta/0.65 equals target - curr on every trial. In monkey M, about half of the MNAV trials have seqq 3, whose vectors come in steps of 0.975 s (0.975 to 4.875 s, printed above), not the 0.65 s the paper describes for both monkeys; the paper and the files do not describe this sequence. Analyses that use distance keep seqq < 3, as the paper's code does for the PI (claims, opening comment). Rows with attempt 99 or 999 have tp 99 or 999 (no production) and are not used.

Spike times and trial times share one range in every session. The eye and joystick timestamps do not in several sessions: they start hundreds of thousands of seconds away from the trial times (A 08152019; M 04122021, 04132021, 04142021, 04212021, 04222021, 04252021, 05062021, 05072021), so in those sessions the behavioural traces are on another clock, which the files do not describe. The eye and joystick traces are used only for claim ed3, in the sessions whose timestamps span the trial times.

The trial table has no fixation or ITI column: start_time equals stim1onttl, the onset of the start landmark. Each row is one trial. On rows with attempt 2 the joystick is pressed as soon after the go cue as on attempt 1 rows (medians printed above), and the row then runs longer after the joystick offset (medians 2.4 to 5.4 s against 0.9 to 1.3 s), with relative errors of about 0.3 to 0.5 against 0.1. This is consistent with the row's tp and joystick times being the first attempt, followed by a second attempt the table does not time; the files do not say so.

In [5]:
# Clock check: the paper's motor response before joystick offset (Extended Data Fig. 10). For each
# session, the fraction of units whose mean rate differs (Welch t-test, p < 0.01) between 0.4-0.1 s
# and 1.0-0.6 s before joystick offset on first-attempt MNAV trials, with the true offset times and
# with the offset times of each trial replaced by those of a trial 5 rows later (a shifted label).
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    tr = s["trials"]
    d = tr[(tr.trial_type == 3) & (tr.attempt == 1) & (tr.tp.abs() > 1.5)]
    off = d.joy1offttl.values
    out = {"monkey": s["monkey"], "session": s["session"], "trials": len(d)}
    for name, t in (("true", off), ("shifted", np.roll(off, 5) + 7.0)):
        sig = 0
        for sp in s["spikes"]:
            late = mnav.mean_rate(sp, t - 0.4, t - 0.1)
            early = mnav.mean_rate(sp, t - 1.0, t - 0.6)
            if np.std(late - early) > 0 and stats.ttest_rel(late, early).pvalue < 0.01:
                sig += 1
        out[f"frac_units_{name}"] = round(sig / len(s["spikes"]), 3)
    rows.append(out)
clock = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(clock.to_string(index=False))

In 12 of the 15 sessions more units change their rate before the true joystick offset than before the shifted times (printed above), which is consistent with spikes and trials sharing a clock there. In three sessions (A 09172019, M 04132021, M 04142021) no unit does so with either timing, and while preparing this notebook the population rate of these sessions was flat (within a few percent) around the stimulus onset, go cue, joystick onset and joystick offset (not run here). In M 04132021 the spikes also stop at 9,306 s while trials run to 18,599 s. For these three sessions a shared clock could not be established; they are kept, as the paper analysed all units, and results are broken down by session where it matters.

fig1bc-produced-matches-actual¶

In MNAV the produced vectors match the actual vectors in direction and magnitude; performance is quantified by the slope of the regression of v_p on v_a.

Criterion (claims file): per recorded session, OLS of signed v_p on signed v_a over all MNAV trials with a recorded production (code: 0.01 < |tp| and tp < 99 s); reproduced when, in each monkey, the median session slope is at least 0.8 and every slope is positive. Variant: the validtrials_mm trials only.

In [6]:
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    tr = s["trials"]
    d = tr[(tr.trial_type == 3) & (tr.tp.abs() > 0.01) & (tr.tp < 99)]
    v = d[d.validtrials_mm == 1]
    fit = stats.linregress(d.ta, d.tp)
    fitv = stats.linregress(v.ta, v.tp)
    rows.append({"monkey": s["monkey"], "session": s["session"], "trials": len(d), "slope_all": fit.slope,
                 "r_all": fit.rvalue, "valid_trials": len(v), "slope_valid": fitv.slope})
fig1 = pd.DataFrame(rows)

Result: reproduced. The median session slope is 0.872 in monkey A (6 sessions, 0.825 to 0.946) and 0.860 in monkey M (9 sessions, 0.687 to 0.893), so at least 0.8 in both, and every slope is positive. One monkey M session (04142021) is below 0.8. On the validtrials_mm trials the medians are 0.936 and 0.869. These are the recorded sessions only, a subset of the behavioural sessions of Fig. 1c.

The periodicity index (PI) of every unit¶

Computed once, as the claims file's opening comment and mnav.py describe, for both lag ranges (Methods 0 to 1,300 ms, code 100 to 1,600 ms), per unit and direction, on first-attempt MNAV trials over at least three landmarks with |tp| > 1 s and seqq < 3.

# Null distributions (Methods: GP surrogate, Poisson, smoothed as the data; 1,000 repeats) and the
# code's variant without the Poisson step ("gp"). The own-duration null of a unit averages as many
# surrogate trials as the unit keeps (k, matched to the nearest level of a grid in steps of 25%),
# with durations drawn from its session and direction's trials. The global null averages the
# monkey's median k trials, all at its median duration, from a bank generated at that duration.
rng_null = np.random.default_rng(897)
LAGSETS = {"methods": mnav.LAGS_METHODS, "code": mnav.LAGS_CODE}
NULL_TYPES = {"poisson": True, "gp": False}

def thresholds(null):
    m, sd = null.mean(0), null.std(0)
    scores = mnav.pi_scores(null)
    return {"per_lag": m + 2 * sd, "a1": float((m + 2 * sd).max()), "a2": float(scores.mean() + 2 * scores.std()),
            "score_mean": float(scores.mean()), "score_sd": float(scores.std())}

kept = pit.k > mnav.MIN_TRIALS
pit["k_level"] = 0
pit.loc[kept, "k_level"] = mnav.k_levels(pit.loc[kept, "k"].values)[1]
thr, banks, surr_rate = {}, {}, {}
t = time.time()
for monkey in ("A", "M"):
    sub = pit[(pit.monkey == monkey)]
    groups = sub.drop_duplicates(["session", "direction"])
    all_durations = np.concatenate(groups.durations.values)
    rates = []
    for s in sessions:
        if s["monkey"] != monkey:
            continue
        trs = mnav.pi_trials(s["trials"])
        t0, t1 = mnav.nav_windows(trs)
        rates += [float(np.mean(mnav.mean_rate(sp, t0, t1))) for sp in s["spikes"]]
    rate = surr_rate[monkey] = float(np.median(rates))
    k_med = int(np.median(sub[sub.k > mnav.MIN_TRIALS].k))
    d_med = float(np.median(all_durations))
    for null_type, poisson in NULL_TYPES.items():
        bank, bank_d = mnav.surrogate_bank(rng_null, all_durations, rate, 4000, poisson=poisson)
        gbank, gbank_d = mnav.surrogate_bank(rng_null, [d_med], rate, 3000, poisson=poisson)
        banks[(monkey, null_type)] = (bank, bank_d)
        for lag, curves in mnav.null_from_bank(rng_null, gbank, gbank_d, [d_med], k_med, LAGSETS).items():
            thr[(monkey, "global", null_type, lag)] = thresholds(curves)
        for _, g in groups.iterrows():
            levels = sub[(sub.session == g.session) & (sub.direction == g.direction) & (sub.k > mnav.MIN_TRIALS)].k_level.unique()
            for lev in levels:
                for lag, curves in mnav.null_from_bank(rng_null, bank, bank_d, g.durations, int(lev), LAGSETS).items():
                    thr[(monkey, g.session, g.direction, int(lev), null_type, lag)] = thresholds(curves)
    print(f"monkey {monkey}: surrogate rate {rate:.2f} spikes/s (median unit rate); global null with {k_med} trials "
          f"of {d_med:.0f} ms; banks of {len(bank)} surrogate trials (durations of the PI trials) and {len(gbank)} (median duration)")
print(f"{len(thr)} nulls in {time.time() - t:.0f} s")
print("Kept trials per unit (k) as a fraction of its session and direction's PI trials, units with k > 15:",
      pit[kept].assign(f=pit.k / pit.n_trials).groupby("monkey").f.quantile([0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75]).round(2).to_dict())

# Classification under every reading. Rules: (a1) score = max PI - mean PI from the first
# positive lag on, above the maximum over lags of the surrogate PI mean + 2 SD; (a2) the same score
# above the surrogate scores' mean + 2 SD; (b) PI at any lag above the surrogate mean + 2 SD at that
# lag. Null durations: own (the session and direction's trials, k-matched) or global. Lags: methods
# or code. Null: poisson (Methods) or gp (code's variant, no Poisson step).
READINGS = [(rule, dur, lag, nt) for nt in NULL_TYPES for rule in ("a1", "a2", "b") for dur in ("own", "global")
            for lag in ("methods", "code")]

def thr_key(row, dur, lag, nt):
    if dur == "global":
        return (row.monkey, "global", nt, lag)
    return (row.monkey, row.session, row.direction, int(row.k_level), nt, lag)

def classify(row, rule, dur, lag, nt):
    pi = getattr(row, "pi_" + lag)
    if pi is None or row.k <= mnav.MIN_TRIALS:
        return False
    th = thr[thr_key(row, dur, lag, nt)]
    if rule == "b":
        return bool(np.any(pi > th["per_lag"]))
    return mnav.pi_score(pi) > th[rule]

def rname(r):
    return "/".join(r)

for r in READINGS:
    pit["per_" + "_".join(r)] = [classify(row, *r) for row in pit.itertuples()]
for lag, lags in LAGSETS.items():
    pit[f"period_{lag}"] = [np.nan if p is None else lags[int(np.argmax(p))] / 1000 for p in pit["pi_" + lag]]
    pit[f"score_{lag}"] = [np.nan if p is None else mnav.pi_score(p) for p in pit["pi_" + lag]]
MAIN = ("a2", "own", "methods", "poisson")
main_col = "per_" + "_".join(MAIN)
# periodic sets carried to the claims that use periodic units: the main reading and the readings
# that differ from it in the rule or the null
SETS = {"a2 (main)": main_col, "a1": "per_a1_own_methods_poisson", "b": "per_b_own_methods_poisson",
        "a2, gp null": "per_a2_own_methods_gp"}
i650 = int(np.nonzero(mnav.LAGS_METHODS == 650)[0][0])
base = pit[["monkey", "session", "unit", "direction", "k", "k_level", "pi_methods", "period_methods", "score_methods"]
           + list(dict.fromkeys(SETS.values()))].copy()
base["above650"] = [False if (p is None or r.k <= mnav.MIN_TRIALS) else
                    p[i650] > thr[thr_key(r, "own", "methods", "poisson")]["per_lag"][i650]
                    for p, r in zip(base.pi_methods, base.itertuples())]
print("Thresholds, global null (rule a1, rule a2; score mean and SD):")
for key in [k for k in thr if k[1] == "global"]:
    print(" ", key, {k: round(v, 3) for k, v in thr[key].items() if k != "per_lag"})
own = pd.DataFrame([{"monkey": k[0], "session": k[1], "direction": k[2], "k_level": k[3], "null": k[4], "lags": k[5],
                     "a1": v["a1"], "a2": v["a2"]} for k, v in thr.items() if k[1] != "global"])
print("\nOwn-duration null thresholds (rule a2), by k level, median over sessions and directions:")
print(own[own.lags == "methods"].pivot_table(index="k_level", columns=["monkey", "null"], values="a2", aggfunc="median").round(3).to_string())
print("\nOwn-duration null thresholds (rule a2, Methods lags, Poisson) per session and direction, range over k levels:")
print(own[(own.lags == "methods") & (own.null == "poisson")].groupby(["monkey", "session", "direction"]).a2
      .agg(["min", "max", "size"]).round(3).to_string())
print("\nNeuron scores (methods lags), median and 90th percentile per monkey:",
      pit[pit.k > mnav.MIN_TRIALS].groupby("monkey").score_methods.quantile([0.5, 0.9]).round(3).to_dict())

# Check of the bank: one group's null built from the bank against a null generated afresh (each
# surrogate trial a new GP and Poisson draw), at the group's largest k level, 300 surrogates.
rng_chk = np.random.default_rng(8970)
g0 = pit[(pit.monkey == "A") & (pit.k > mnav.MIN_TRIALS)].sort_values(["session", "direction"]).iloc[0]
lev = int(pit[(pit.session == g0.session) & (pit.direction == g0.direction) & (pit.k > mnav.MIN_TRIALS)].k_level.max())
t = time.time()
fresh = mnav.surrogate_pis(rng_chk, g0.durations, lev, surr_rate["A"], mnav.LAGS_METHODS, n=300)
bank, bank_d = banks[("A", "poisson")]
from_bank = mnav.null_from_bank(rng_chk, bank, bank_d, g0.durations, lev, {"methods": mnav.LAGS_METHODS})["methods"]
for name, null in (("fresh", fresh), ("bank", from_bank), ("bank, as used", None)):
    th = thresholds(null) if null is not None else thr[("A", g0.session, g0.direction, lev, "poisson", "methods")]
    print(f"monkey A {g0.session} direction {int(g0.direction)}, k = {lev}, {name}: a2 threshold {th['a2']:.3f} "
          f"(score mean {th['score_mean']:.3f}, SD {th['score_sd']:.3f}); a1 threshold {th['a1']:.3f}; "
          f"per-lag threshold at 650 ms {th['per_lag'][i650]:.3f}")
print(f"in {time.time() - t:.0f} s")

The nulls are now drawn at random from the whole neighbourhood of 200 bank entries nearest in duration (all entries for the global null, whose bank is generated at the median duration), and each unit's own-duration null averages as many surrogate trials as the unit keeps (k). Units keep a median of 68 to 69% of their session and direction's PI trials (10th percentile 20%), and the a2 threshold falls from about 0.36 (A) and 0.29 (M) at k = 16 to 0.14 to 0.15 at the largest k (printed above), so matching k matters. For one group the bank null gives an a2 threshold of 0.155 (0.152 as used) against 0.141 for a null generated afresh, a difference of about 0.4 SD of the null scores (0.03), so the bank thresholds are slightly conservative.

fig2-periodic-proportion¶

A substantial fraction of EC neurons have significantly periodic activity during mental navigation, 37% (231/614) in monkey A and 36% (311/864) in monkey M, and the proportion per session ranged from 0% to 45% depending on recording site.

A unit counts as periodic when it is periodic in either direction; the denominator is all units of the monkey. The dandiset holds 6 of the 17 monkey A sessions and 9 of the 15 monkey M sessions, so the counts cannot reach 231 and 311; they are compared as proportions of the units the dandiset holds (231/614 and 311/864, each with the claims file's 10% relative tolerance), and the raw counts are printed.

units_total = info.groupby("monkey").units.sum()

paper = {"A": (231, 614), "M": (311, 864)}
labels = pit.drop_duplicates(["monkey", "session", "unit"])[["monkey", "session", "unit", "label"]]
rows, sess_rows = [], []
for r in READINGS:
    col = "per_" + "_".join(r)
    per_unit = pit.groupby(["monkey", "session", "unit"])[col].any().reset_index()
    out = {"reading": rname(r)}
    for m in ("A", "M"):
        n = int(per_unit[per_unit.monkey == m][col].sum())
        p_ref = paper[m][0] / paper[m][1]
        out[f"{m}_count"] = n
        out[f"{m}_pct"] = round(100 * n / units_total[m], 1)
        nn = per_unit[(per_unit.monkey == m)].merge(labels, on=["monkey", "session", "unit"])
        nn = nn[nn.label != "noise"]
        out[f"{m}_pct_no_noise"] = round(100 * nn[col].mean(), 1)
        out[f"{m}_in_tol"] = abs(n / units_total[m] - p_ref) <= 0.1 * p_ref
    ses = per_unit.groupby("session")[col].mean() * 100
    out["session_pct_min"] = round(ses.min(), 1)
    out["session_pct_max"] = round(ses.max(), 1)
    out["sessions_in_0_49.5"] = bool((ses <= 49.5).all())
    out["conditions_met"] = int(out["A_in_tol"]) + int(out["M_in_tol"]) + int(out["sessions_in_0_49.5"])
    rows.append(out)
    sess_rows.append(ses.rename(rname(r)))

Result: not reproduced, resting on an assumption. Under no reading is either monkey's proportion within 10% of the paper's (A 37.6%, M 36.0%). Under the main reading (rule a2, own-duration null matched to each unit's kept trials, Methods lags, Poisson null) 56 of 364 units in monkey A (15.4%) and 57 of 729 in monkey M (7.8%) are periodic, with session proportions of 1.0% to 30.6%. The a2 readings give 7.1% to 31.3% (A) and 0.1% to 7.8% (M); a1 at most 5.2% and 0.4%; b 65.7% to 81.3% and 52.0% to 60.4%, with session maxima of 73.9% to 95.3%, above 49.5%. Only the per-session range is met, under the a1 and a2 readings, so at most one of the three conditions holds under any reading. The code's GP null without the Poisson step gives fewer periodic units than the Methods' null under a1 and a2 (A 1.1% to 16.2%, M 0% to 5.8%). Without units labelled noise, the main reading gives 20.7% in monkey A; without the three sessions whose clock could not be checked, 15.3% (A, 46/300) and 9.0% (M, 47/524). The conversion of the GP into a firing rate is an assumption (mnav.py), and the counts are judged as proportions because the dandiset holds 15 of the 32 sessions.

fig2d-periodicity-at-065¶

Across neurons with significant PI, the lag of the peak PI was at or near 0.65 s, the temporal distance between landmarks.

Criterion: median periodicity (lag of the maximum PI) of the periodic units within 0.60 to 0.70 s in every monkey and direction; the mode in 50 ms bins is reported as well.

Result: partially reproduced, resting on an assumption. Under the main reading the median periodicity of the periodic units is 0.580 s (A, direction -1), 0.590 s (A, 1), 0.650 s (M, -1) and 0.640 s (M, 1): within 0.60 to 0.70 s in the two monkey M groups and not in monkey A. The a2 readings put 0 to 4 of the groups within the range (4 of 4 with the global null and the Poisson null, 0 of 3 with the own-duration GP null and the code's lags); under a1, which selects 0 to 14 units per group, 0 or 1; under b, which selects most units, 0 or 1, with medians of 0.695 to 0.96 s, close to those of all units (0.73 to 0.91 s). The readings disagree; reading a2 is adopted, as it compares the code's score with the same score on the surrogates. Pooling all periodic unit-directions of the main reading, the median is 0.63 s.

ed2c-pi-error-below-correct¶

Neurons significantly periodic at 0.65 s had a lower PI on error trials than on correct trials, suggesting weaker periodicity contributed to larger errors.

PI measure (claims, ed2b and ed2c): PI at the 650 ms lag minus the mean PI from the first lag at which PI is positive. Correct trials are the PI trials; error trials are the first attempt of trials with more than one attempt (attempt == 2; Methods, MNAV; the data check shows the row's joystick times are the first attempt's), with the same distance, |tp| and seqq rules; the code's variant takes succ == 0 trials with |tp| > 1.8 s. Neurons, two readings: (i) code, periodic units whose PI at 650 ms exceeds the surrogate PI mean + 2 SD at 650 ms; (ii) Results, periodic units with periodicity in 0.60 to 0.70 s. Periodic units are those of each periodic set (the main reading and the a1, b and GP-null readings). Both conditions need more than 15 trials. One-tailed paired t-test, correct > error. As a control for the number of trials (correct trials outnumber error trials, and a mean ACG over fewer trials is noisier), the main reading is also run with the correct trials of each session and direction subsampled at random to the number of error trials.

In [13]:
def pi650_measure(pi, lags=mnav.LAGS_METHODS):
    i650 = int(np.nonzero(lags == 650)[0][0])
    pos = np.nonzero(pi > 0)[0]
    base_ = pi[pos[0]:].mean() if len(pos) else pi.mean()
    return float(pi[i650] - base_)

rng2c = np.random.default_rng(2002)

def matched_correct(tr):
    """Control for trial count: per direction, a random subset of the correct PI trials as large as
    the error PI trials (Methods' error trials)."""
    out = pd.Series(False, index=tr.index)
    for d in (1, -1):
        c = mnav.pi_trials(tr, d)
        e = mnav.pi_trials(tr, d, attempt=2)
        out[rng2c.choice(c.index, min(len(c), len(e)), replace=False)] = True
    return out

t = time.time()
pit_err = mnav.periodicity_table(sessions, attempt=2, lag_sets={"methods": mnav.LAGS_METHODS})
pit_err_code = mnav.periodicity_table(
    sessions, attempt=2, lag_sets={"methods": mnav.LAGS_METHODS},
    extra=lambda tr: (tr.succ == 0) & (tr.tp.abs() > 1.8))
pit_cmatch = mnav.periodicity_table(sessions, extra=matched_correct, lag_sets={"methods": mnav.LAGS_METHODS})
print(f"error-trial and matched correct-trial PI in {time.time() - t:.0f} s")
rows = []
for set_name, set_col in SETS.items():
    for err_name, err in (("attempt2", pit_err), ("code_succ0_tp1.8", pit_err_code)):
        for corr_name in ("all correct", "correct matched to error count"):
            if corr_name != "all correct" and (err_name != "attempt2" or set_name != "a2 (main)"):
                continue
            mrg = base.merge(err[["monkey", "session", "unit", "direction", "k", "pi_methods"]],
                             on=["monkey", "session", "unit", "direction"], suffixes=("", "_err"))
            if corr_name != "all correct":
                mrg = mrg.drop(columns=["k", "pi_methods"]).merge(
                    pit_cmatch[["monkey", "session", "unit", "direction", "k", "pi_methods"]], on=["monkey", "session", "unit", "direction"])
            for sel_name, sel in (("i_code_pi650", mrg[set_col] & mrg.above650),
                                  ("ii_results_0.6-0.7", mrg[set_col] & mrg.period_methods.between(0.6, 0.7))):
                g = mrg[sel & (mrg.k_err > mnav.MIN_TRIALS) & (mrg.k > mnav.MIN_TRIALS)]
                for (m, d), gg in g.groupby(["monkey", "direction"]):
                    c = np.array([pi650_measure(p) for p in gg.pi_methods])
                    e = np.array([pi650_measure(p) for p in gg.pi_methods_err])
                    tt = stats.ttest_rel(c, e, alternative="greater") if len(gg) > 1 else None
                    rows.append({"periodic_set": set_name, "error_trials": err_name, "correct_trials": corr_name, "neurons": sel_name,
                                 "monkey": m, "direction": int(d), "n": len(gg),
                                 "dropped_<=15_trials": int((sel & (mrg.monkey == m) & (mrg.direction == d)).sum() - len(gg)),
                                 "k_correct_median": int(np.median(gg.k)), "k_error_median": int(np.median(gg.k_err)),
                                 "correct_mean": round(c.mean(), 3), "error_mean": round(e.mean(), 3),
                                 "t": None if tt is None else round(tt.statistic, 2), "p_one_tailed": None if tt is None else tt.pvalue,
                                 "meets_p<1e-4": bool(tt is not None and tt.pvalue < 1e-4 and c.mean() > e.mean())})
ed2c = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(ed2c.to_string(index=False))
print("\nGroups meeting the criterion per reading (of 4; groups with fewer than 2 neurons are not tested):")
print(ed2c.groupby(["periodic_set", "error_trials", "correct_trials", "neurons"], sort=False)["meets_p<1e-4"].agg(["sum", "size"]).to_string())

Result: not reproduced, resting on an assumption. Under the main reading, with the Methods' error trials, correct-trial PI exceeds error-trial PI in all four groups (0.203 to 0.319 against 0.121 to 0.225 under the code's neuron selection), but p < 0.0001 in only 1 of 4 groups under either neuron selection (code: A -1, t = 4.80, n = 18, while A 1, M -1 and M 1 have p = 0.0018, 0.0119 and 0.00010; Results: M 1, t = 5.05, n = 26). With the correct trials subsampled to the error-trial count, no group reaches it (p 2.0e-04 to 0.14). The other readings differ: with the code's error trials, 2 of 4 groups under the code's selection, and 4 of 4 under rule b with the Results' selection; under rule a1 too few units are periodic (2 to 7 per group in monkey A, none in M). The groups hold 10 to 26 neurons under the main reading against the paper's 66 to 104.

ed4d-overshoot-longer-period¶

For trials of the same desired distance, the periodicity of EC neurons is significantly longer (lower frequency) on overshoot trials (top tertile of produced vector) than on undershoot trials (bottom tertile).

Periodic units (each periodic set: the main reading and the a1, b and GP-null readings), per direction in which they are periodic; correct trials of distance 3 (with the PI rules); per session and direction, trials sorted by |tp| - |ta|, bottom and top tertiles; periodicity (Methods lags) on each; units with fewer than 15 kept trials in a tertile dropped, and periodicities of 0 or above 1 s dropped. Rank-sum test of overshoot against undershoot across units, per monkey; the code's variant lags (100 to 1,090 ms) are also shown.

In [14]:
def tertile_mask(which):
    def f(tr):
        m = (tr.trial_type == 3) & (tr.attempt == 1) & (tr.distance == 3) & (tr.tp.abs() > 1) & (tr.seqq < 3)
        out = pd.Series(False, index=tr.index)
        for d in (1, -1):
            g = tr[m & (tr.direction == d)]
            err = g.tp.abs() - g.ta.abs()
            lo, hi = err.quantile(1 / 3), err.quantile(2 / 3)
            out[g.index[err <= lo] if which == "under" else g.index[err >= hi]] = True
        return out
    return f

lagsets = {"methods": mnav.LAGS_METHODS, "code": np.arange(100, 1091, 10)}
t = time.time()
under = mnav.periodicity_table(sessions, extra=tertile_mask("under"), lag_sets=lagsets)
over = mnav.periodicity_table(sessions, extra=tertile_mask("over"), lag_sets=lagsets)
print(f"tertile PI in {time.time() - t:.0f} s")
rows = []
for (set_name, set_col), (lag, lags) in [(sc, ll) for sc in SETS.items() for ll in lagsets.items()]:
    mrg = under.merge(over, on=["monkey", "session", "unit", "direction"], suffixes=("_u", "_o"))
    mrg = mrg.merge(base[["monkey", "session", "unit", "direction", set_col]], on=["monkey", "session", "unit", "direction"])
    mrg = mrg[mrg[set_col]]
    n_periodic = mrg.groupby("monkey").size()
    ok = (mrg.k_u >= 15) & (mrg.k_o >= 15) & mrg[f"pi_{lag}_u"].notna() & mrg[f"pi_{lag}_o"].notna()
    mrg = mrg[ok].copy()
    mrg["per_u"] = [lags[int(np.argmax(p))] / 1000 for p in mrg[f"pi_{lag}_u"]]
    mrg["per_o"] = [lags[int(np.argmax(p))] / 1000 for p in mrg[f"pi_{lag}_o"]]
    keep = (mrg.per_u > 0) & (mrg.per_u <= 1) & (mrg.per_o > 0) & (mrg.per_o <= 1)
    for m in ("A", "M"):
        g = mrg[keep & (mrg.monkey == m)]
        if len(g) < 2:
            rows.append({"periodic_set": set_name, "lags": lag, "monkey": m, "n": len(g)})
            continue
        rs = stats.ranksums(g.per_o, g.per_u)
        rows.append({"periodic_set": set_name, "lags": lag, "monkey": m, "periodic_unit_dirs": int(n_periodic.get(m, 0)),
                     "kept_>=15_trials": int((mrg.monkey == m).sum()), "n": len(g),
                     "median_under_s": g.per_u.median(), "median_over_s": g.per_o.median(),
                     "mean_diff_over-under_s": round((g.per_o - g.per_u).mean(), 4),
                     "ranksum_Z(over-under)": round(rs.statistic, 2), "p": rs.pvalue,
                     "meets(over>under,p<0.05)": bool(rs.pvalue < 0.05 and g.per_o.median() >= g.per_u.median() and rs.statistic > 0)})
ed4d = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(ed4d.to_string(index=False))
print("Trials per tertile per session and direction (median):",
      int(np.median([len(d) for d in under.drop_duplicates(['session', 'direction']).durations])))

Result: partially reproduced, resting on an assumption. Under the main reading, in monkey M the overshoot tertile has a longer periodicity (median 0.71 against 0.58 s, rank-sum Z = 3.83, p = 1.3e-04, n = 29 unit-directions); in monkey A the difference is in the same direction but not significant (0.590 against 0.570 s, Z = 0.78, p = 0.43, n = 41). The code's lag range gives the same (M p = 1.1e-04, n = 30). Rule b gives the same split (M p = 3.4e-07, A p = 0.15); rule a1 has no periodic units in monkey M, and the GP-null reading leaves 1 in M; neither reaches p < 0.05 in A (p = 0.66 and 0.25). Of the periodic unit-directions of the main reading, 45 of 68 (A) and 34 of 64 (M) had at least 15 trials in both tertiles.

ed10-motor-preparation-signal¶

Most EC neurons show a motor-related response before joystick offset, 77% (477/614) in monkey A and 70% (607/864) in monkey M, including most non-periodic neurons (81%, 368/452, in A and 89%, 432/481, in M).

Criterion (claims, from the code): direction 1, first-attempt MNAV trials of distance at least 3 with |tp| > 1.5 s, at least 6 trials; spike-count rate in tp - 1 to tp - 0.6 s and in tp - 0.4 to tp - 0.1 s after joystick onset; 200 bootstrap means of each; two-sample t-test at p < 0.0001 (two-sided; increase only as a variant). Non-periodic: not periodic (each periodic set) with more than 15 PI trials. As for fig2, the dandiset holds a subset of the sessions, so the counts are compared as proportions of the units it holds; the raw counts are printed. Variants: either direction, and a paired t-test across the trials themselves (without the bootstrap, whose t-test on 200 resampled means has a p-value that shrinks with the number of resamples).

In [15]:
rng10 = np.random.default_rng(10)
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    tr = s["trials"]
    for d in (1, -1):
        g = tr[(tr.trial_type == 3) & (tr.attempt == 1) & (tr.distance >= 3) & (tr.tp.abs() > 1.5) & (tr.seqq < 3) & (tr.direction == d)]
        on, tp = g.joy1onttl.values, g.tp.abs().values
        for u, sp in enumerate(s["spikes"]):
            row = {"monkey": s["monkey"], "session": s["session"], "unit": u, "direction": d, "n": len(g)}
            if len(g) >= 6:
                early = mnav.mean_rate(sp, on + tp - 1.0, on + tp - 0.6)
                late = mnav.mean_rate(sp, on + tp - 0.4, on + tp - 0.1)
                idx = rng10.integers(0, len(g), size=(200, len(g)))
                be, bl = early[idx].mean(1), late[idx].mean(1)
                p = stats.ttest_ind(bl, be).pvalue if (be.std() + bl.std()) > 0 else 1.0
                # variant without the bootstrap: paired t-test across the trials themselves
                p_tr = stats.ttest_rel(late, early).pvalue if np.std(late - early) > 0 else 1.0
                row.update(p=p, p_trials=p_tr, increase=bl.mean() > be.mean())
            rows.append(row)

Result: partially reproduced, resting on an assumption. Under the code's test (two-sided, direction 1), 75.5% of the monkey A units (275/364) and 67.9% of the monkey M units (495/729) are motor-related, within 10% of the paper's 77.7% and 70.3%. Under the main periodic reading, 65.9% (A, 240/364) and 52.8% (M, 385/729) of the units are non-periodic, against 73.6% and 55.7%: M is within 10% and A just outside (the bound is 66.2%). Among them 84.6% (203/240) and 83.6% (322/385) are motor-related, within 10% of 81.4% and 89.8%. So five of the six values are within tolerance, and the four proportions are each above 50%. Under the a1 and GP-null readings all six are within tolerance (non-periodic 78.6% and 72.5% in A, 60.6% and 59.5% in M); under b too few units are non-periodic (15.7% and 8.6%). The test says little about a motor signal: counting increases only gives 33.0% and 33.1%, and a paired t-test across the trials themselves at p < 0.0001 finds 5.8% (A) and 6.9% (M) of the units; in M 04142021 and A 09172019, where no clock check succeeded, the bootstrap test still finds 47.3% and 76.6%.

Ramping and distance coding: shared selection¶

Correct (first-attempt) MNAV trials with seqq < 3 (distance from ta in 0.65 s steps). Units with at least 10 such trials per distance (1 to 5) in both directions (claims, fig3b and fig3d, from the code); direction 1 (ta > 0) is analysed (code line 93).

In [16]:
def coding_trials(tr):
    return tr[(tr.trial_type == 3) & (tr.attempt == 1) & (tr.seqq < 3) & (tr.tp.abs() > 0.01) & (tr.tp < 99)]

sel_rows = []
for s in sessions:
    g = coding_trials(s["trials"])
    cnt = g.groupby(["direction", "distance"]).size()
    ok = all(cnt.get((d, k), 0) >= 10 for d in (1, -1) for k in range(1, 6))
    sel_rows.append({"monkey": s["monkey"], "session": s["session"], "min_trials_per_dir_dist": int(cnt.min()), "eligible": ok,
                     "units": len(s["spikes"])})
elig = pd.DataFrame(sel_rows)
print(elig.to_string(index=False))
print("Eligible units per monkey:", elig[elig.eligible].groupby("monkey").units.sum().to_dict())

fig3b-onset-and-offset-coding¶

Single EC neurons encode temporal distance in their firing rate before joystick onset, before joystick offset, or, in a small number, at both.

Cross-validated R2 (Methods, Cross-validated R2; claims): mean rate in the window, each distance subsampled to the smallest count, random halves, linear fit of rate on distance 1 to 5 on the training half scored on the held-out half, 50 splits averaged; positive coding is mean R2 > 0; units with R2 below -1 dropped. Windows: (a) 100 ms before onset and offset, (b) 200 ms before. Null: the same with the distances shuffled.

In [17]:
rng3b = np.random.default_rng(3)

def cv_r2(y, x, rng, n_split=50, shuffle=False):
    out = []
    for _ in range(n_split):
        xx = rng.permutation(x) if shuffle else x
        perm = rng.permutation(len(y))
        tr_i, te_i = perm[: len(y) // 2], perm[len(y) // 2:]
        b = np.polyfit(xx[tr_i], y[tr_i], 1)
        pred = np.polyval(b, xx[te_i])
        yt = y[te_i]
        ss = np.sum((yt - yt.mean()) ** 2)
        out.append(1 - np.sum((yt - pred) ** 2) / ss if ss > 0 else np.nan)
    return np.nanmean(out) if np.any(np.isfinite(out)) else np.nan

rows = []
for s in sessions:
    if not elig.set_index("session").eligible[s["session"]]:
        continue
    g = coding_trials(s["trials"])
    g = g[g.direction == 1]
    nmin = g.groupby("distance").size().loc[1:5].min()
    g = pd.concat([gg.sample(nmin, random_state=int(rng3b.integers(1e9))) for k, gg in g.groupby("distance") if 1 <= k <= 5])
    x = g.distance.values.astype(float)
    on, off = g.joy1onttl.values, g.joy1offttl.values
    for u, sp in enumerate(s["spikes"]):
        row = {"monkey": s["monkey"], "session": s["session"], "unit": u}
        for w in (0.1, 0.2):
            for ev, t in (("onset", on), ("offset", off)):
                y = mnav.mean_rate(sp, t - w, t)
                row[f"r2_{ev}_{int(w * 1000)}"] = cv_r2(y, x, rng3b)
                row[f"r2shuf_{ev}_{int(w * 1000)}"] = cv_r2(y, x, rng3b, shuffle=True)
        rows.append(row)

        on, off = g[f"r2_onset_{w}"], g[f"r2_offset_{w}"]
        valid = (on >= -1) & (off >= -1)
        on, off = on[valid], off[valid]
        son, soff = g[f"r2shuf_onset_{w}"][valid], g[f"r2shuf_offset_{w}"][valid]
        p_on_only = float(((on > 0) & (off <= 0)).mean())
        p_off_only = float(((off > 0) & (on <= 0)).mean())
        p_both = float(((on > 0) & (off > 0)).mean())
        p_shuf = float(((son > 0) | (soff > 0)).mean())
        p_shuf_on, p_shuf_off = float((son > 0).mean()), float((soff > 0).mean())
        res.append({"window_ms": w, "monkey": m, "units": int(valid.sum()), "dropped_r2<-1": int((~valid).sum()),
                    "onset_only": round(p_on_only, 3), "offset_only": round(p_off_only, 3), "both": round(p_both, 3),
                    "shuffled_onset>0": round(p_shuf_on, 3), "shuffled_offset>0": round(p_shuf_off, 3),
                    "meets": bool(p_on_only > p_shuf_on and p_off_only > p_shuf_off and p_both < p_on_only and p_both < p_off_only)})

Result: reproduced. In both monkeys and both windows, the proportions of units coding distance at onset only (A 0.7% and 1.0%, M 8.0% and 8.2% for 100 and 200 ms) and at offset only (A 8.3% and 6.0%, M 2.3% and 3.6%) exceed the proportion with positive cross-validated R2 under the shuffled regressor (0 in every case), and fewer units code at both (A 0%, M 1.1% and 2.9%) than at either alone. The shuffled proportions are 0 because R2 averaged over 50 held-out halves is always negative for a shuffled regressor, so this comparison is weak; the coding proportions themselves are small. Units with R2 below -1 were dropped (A 76 and 63, M 201 and 185). Monkey M sessions with fewer than 10 trials per distance in a direction (3 of 9) are not used.

fig3d-offset-coding-stronger¶

At the population level distance is encoded weakly before joystick onset and robustly and linearly before joystick offset; offset R2 exceeds onset R2 in both monkeys.

Targeted dimensionality reduction (Methods; claims): pseudo-population of each monkey's eligible units, direction 1. Per resample, each unit's trials of each distance are split at random into halves. Rates in 20 ms bins (a standard choice for the time resolution of the regression, which the Methods do not give) in the windows -200 to 0 ms before onset and -500 to -300 ms before offset (Methods); per bin, the regression r = beta * dist across training trials; the axis is the coefficient vector at the bin of largest norm; held-out trials of each distance are averaged, averaged over the window and projected on the axis; R2 of a linear fit of the projections on distance; 50 resamples. Two-sided rank-sum test of offset against onset R2.

Centring, two readings. The Methods centre each unit "by subtracting its mean response across the two windows of interest" and regress without an intercept; a difference between the unit's mean rates in the two windows then loads onto beta. The method the Methods cite for the regression (ref. 63, Mante et al. 2013) has a constant term at each time point, which is equivalent to centring each unit in each window and time bin. Both are run ("windows", the main reading, as the Methods state it, and "bins", a variant). The bin of largest norm is found in each window separately, which the Methods leave open. The criterion's variant with the code's windows (-200 to -100 ms and -400 to -300 ms on time-warped bins) is not run. Other variants: the coefficients projected onto the principal components holding 80% of the training variance (the code's denoising), and distances 2 to 5 only (the Methods' control for distance 1).

rng3d = np.random.default_rng(33)
BIN = 0.02
win = {"onset": (-0.2, 0.0), "offset": (-0.5, -0.3)}
pop = {"A": [], "M": []}
for s in sessions:
    if not elig.set_index("session").eligible[s["session"]]:
        continue
    g = coding_trials(s["trials"])
    g = g[(g.direction == 1) & g.distance.between(1, 5)]
    for u, sp in enumerate(s["spikes"]):
        unit = {}
        for ev, col in (("onset", "joy1onttl"), ("offset", "joy1offttl")):
            a, b = win[ev]
            edges = np.arange(a, b + 1e-9, BIN)
            t = g[col].values
            unit[ev] = np.stack([mnav.mean_rate(sp, t + e0, t + e0 + BIN) for e0 in edges[:-1]], axis=1)  # trials x bins
        unit["dist"] = g.distance.values.astype(int)
        pop[s["monkey"]].append(unit)

def tdr_once(units, rng, denoise=False, centring="windows", dists=(1, 2, 3, 4, 5)):
    """One resample. centring "windows": each unit's training mean across both windows (Methods,
    TDR: "subtracting its mean response across the two windows"); "bins": its training mean in
    each window and time bin (variant). dists: the distances used (the Methods' control leaves out 1)."""
    dists = list(dists)
    train = {"onset": [], "offset": []}
    test = {"onset": [], "offset": []}
    for unit in units:
        tr_idx, te_idx = [], []
        for k in dists:
            idx = rng.permutation(np.nonzero(unit["dist"] == k)[0])
            tr_idx.append(idx[: len(idx) // 2])
            te_idx.append(idx[len(idx) // 2:])
        tr_all = np.concatenate(tr_idx)
        mu = np.mean([unit[ev][tr_all].mean() for ev in ("onset", "offset")])
        for ev in ("onset", "offset"):
            X = unit[ev] - (mu if centring == "windows" else unit[ev][tr_all].mean(0))
            train[ev].append([X[i] for i in tr_idx])
            test[ev].append(np.array([X[i].mean() for i in te_idx]))   # per distance, averaged over bins and trials
    out = {}
    for ev in ("onset", "offset"):
        nb = train[ev][0][0].shape[1]
        beta = np.zeros((len(units), nb))
        cond = np.zeros((len(units), len(dists) * nb))
        for i, per_d in enumerate(train[ev]):
            num = sum(k * per_d[j].sum(0) for j, k in enumerate(dists))
            den = sum(k ** 2 * len(per_d[j]) for j, k in enumerate(dists))
            beta[i] = num / den
            cond[i] = np.concatenate([per_d[j].mean(0) for j in range(len(dists))])
        if denoise:
            c = cond - cond.mean(1, keepdims=True)
            U, S, _ = np.linalg.svd(c, full_matrices=False)
            npc = int(np.searchsorted(np.cumsum(S ** 2) / np.sum(S ** 2), 0.8) + 1)
            beta = U[:, :npc] @ (U[:, :npc].T @ beta)
        tstar = int(np.argmax(np.linalg.norm(beta, axis=0)))
        axis = beta[:, tstar] / np.linalg.norm(beta[:, tstar])
        proj = np.array(test[ev]).T @ axis       # one value per distance
        fit = stats.linregress(dists, proj)
        out[ev] = fit.rvalue ** 2
    return out

rows = []
for centring, dists, denoise in [("windows", (1, 2, 3, 4, 5), False), ("windows", (1, 2, 3, 4, 5), True),
                                 ("bins", (1, 2, 3, 4, 5), False), ("bins", (1, 2, 3, 4, 5), True),
                                 ("windows", (2, 3, 4, 5), False), ("bins", (2, 3, 4, 5), False)]:
    for m in ("A", "M"):

            continue

Mean over units of the offset-window rate minus the onset-window rate (spikes/s): {'A': np.float64(-0.81), 'M': np.float64(1.36)}

Result: partially reproduced. With each unit centred by its mean across the two windows, as the Methods state ("We first centred the responses of each neuron by subtracting its mean response across the two windows of interest before joystick onset and offset"), offset R2 exceeds onset R2 at p < 0.0001 in monkey A (p = 2.8e-07, denoised 5.2e-14) and monkey M reverses (onset 0.787 against offset 0.684, Z = 6.85, p = 7.3e-12; denoised 6.6e-11). With the distances 1 to 5 of the criterion this holds in one monkey, which the criterion calls partially reproduced. Without distance 1, the Methods' control and outside the criterion, A no longer differs (p = 0.91) and M gives offset above onset (p = 4.9e-12).

With the variant centring per window and time bin (the cited method's constant term), offset R2 exceeds onset R2 in both monkeys: A medians 0.853 against 0.502 (Z = -6.03, p = 1.6e-09), M 0.935 against 0.808 (Z = -6.90, p = 5.2e-12); with denoising p = 4.2e-08 and 4.0e-14, and without distance 1 p = 2.4e-11 and 4.2e-14. The mean rate in the offset window is 1.36 spikes/s above the onset window in M and 0.81 below it in A, the difference that the Methods' centring loads onto the coefficients. The bin width of the regression (20 ms) is a standard choice.

ed4fg-distance-over-landmark and ed4e-rate-codes-distance-over-slope: the ANOVAs¶

Four-way ANOVA (distance, start landmark, target landmark, direction; Methods), per unit with at least 10 correct trials in each of the 30 start and target conditions (claims, from the code's landmark ANOVA), on the mean rate (spike count over the window) and on the slope of a line fitted to the smoothed rate in the window. Type II sums of squares (each factor adjusted for the others; the Methods do not say which, a standard choice). Units with zero variance in a window are skipped.

In [19]:
def anova_F(df, y):
    model = smf.ols(f"{y} ~ C(distance) + C(curr) + C(target) + C(direction)", data=df).fit()
    a = sm.stats.anova_lm(model, typ=2)
    return {f: (a.loc[f"C({f})", "F"], a.loc[f"C({f})", "PR(>F)"]) for f in ("distance", "curr", "target", "direction")}

def slope_of(sp, t0, t1):
    rates = mnav.smoothed_rates(sp, t0, t1)
    return np.array([np.polyfit(np.arange(len(r)) / 1000, r, 1)[0] if len(r) > 2 else np.nan for r in rates])

WINDOWS = {"rate_-500_-300": ("rate", -0.5, -0.3), "rate_-200_0": ("rate", -0.2, 0.0), "rate_-400_-300": ("rate", -0.4, -0.3),
           "rate_-550_-250": ("rate", -0.55, -0.25), "slope_-550_-250": ("slope", -0.55, -0.25), "slope_-300_0": ("slope", -0.3, 0.0)}

anova_sessions = []
for s in sessions:
    g = coding_trials(s["trials"])
    cnt = g.groupby(["curr", "target"]).size()
    if len(cnt) < 30 or cnt.min() < 10:
        anova_sessions.append({"session": s["session"], "monkey": s["monkey"], "conditions": len(cnt), "min_trials": int(cnt.min()), "used": False})
        continue
    anova_sessions.append({"session": s["session"], "monkey": s["monkey"], "conditions": len(cnt), "min_trials": int(cnt.min()), "used": True})
    off = g.joy1offttl.values
    for u, sp in enumerate(s["spikes"]):
        row = {"monkey": s["monkey"], "session": s["session"], "unit": u}
        df = g[["distance", "curr", "target", "direction"]].copy()
        for name, (kind, a, b) in WINDOWS.items():
            y = mnav.mean_rate(sp, off + a, off + b) if kind == "rate" else slope_of(sp, off + a, off + b)
            if np.nanstd(y) == 0:
                continue
            df["y"] = y
            res_ = anova_F(df.dropna(), "y")
            for f, (F, p) in res_.items():
                row[f"{name}_{f}_F"] = F
                row[f"{name}_{f}_p"] = p
        rows.append(row)
anova = pd.DataFrame(rows)

ed4fg-distance-over-landmark¶

Significantly less variance of firing rate near joystick offset is explained by the start or the target landmark than by distance.

Units with a significant effect (p < 0.05) of distance or of the landmark; distance F against landmark F, by (a) a t-test on the differences (Methods; paired) and (b) a two-sample t-test (legend). Windows (a) -500 to -300 ms (Methods), (b) the last 200 ms (legend); the code's -400 to -300 ms is a variant.

Result: partially reproduced. In the last 200 ms (legend window) with the t-test on differences (Methods), all four monkey and landmark comparisons meet it (p 6.8e-05 to 3.8e-17); in -500 to -300 ms (Methods window) only monkey M's start landmark does (p 1.4e-04 to 4.5e-03 for the others). Monkey M sessions with fewer than 10 trials in a condition (4 of 9) are not used.

Near joystick offset the distance effect on the mean firing rate is significantly larger than that on the slope of the firing rate.

The inter-trial interval (claims ed2b, fig3e)¶

The paper compares the navigation epoch with ITI segments longer than 4 s (Methods, NTS). The trial table has no ITI or fixation event: each row starts at the stimulus onset and stops at the next row's start. The only interval that can hold the ITI is from the joystick offset to the next trial's start, printed here.

Every row ends where the next begins, and the time from a completed trial's joystick offset to the next trial's start is about 0.9 s (A) or 1.2 s (M), longer than 4 s in 0 to 6 trials per session. After aborted trials (the Methods add a 5 s time-out) the next trial starts a median 6.1 to 6.3 s after the abort in monkey M sessions and 2.3 to 2.4 s in monkey A (printed for each session above); the paper does not say that its ITI segments came from there. The ITI segments longer than 4 s that claims ed2b and fig3e use cannot be located in the files, so those claims are not tested. Claim ed5 uses the selection of fig3e but none of its comparisons uses the ITI, so it is tested below.

ed5-xcorr-conserved-other-epochs¶

The conserved correlation structure generalizes to the inference epoch, error trials and both directions of movement.

This claim's comparisons do not use the ITI: the navigation epoch against the inference epoch (first image onset -0.2 to 1.2 s), against error trials (first attempt of two-attempt trials, the same window as navigation) and between the two directions. Selection as fig3e: the session readings are the chronological fifth monkey A and first monkey M session among the sessions the dandiset holds (the paper's list holds more sessions, so these need not be the paper's) and every session with at least 20 periodic units (main reading); the 20 (legend) or 25 (code) units with the highest PI score. Per pair, the trial-averaged normalised cross-correlation of the detrended smoothed rates (as for the PI), averaged over lags -5 to 5 ms; navigation trials are first-attempt MNAV trials of distance above 3, from joystick onset to 500 ms before offset. Pearson r across pairs; the p-value at lag 0 is Bonferroni-corrected over the lags of Extended Data Fig. 5c (-900 to 900 ms), counted as 1,801 lags (1 ms steps, the stricter) and as 181 (10 ms steps).

In [23]:
sess_by = {s["session"]: s for s in sessions}
rng5 = np.random.default_rng(55)

def pair_xcorr(sp_list, t0, t1, max_lag=5):
    """Per pair of units, the trial-averaged normalised cross-correlation of the detrended smoothed
    rates, averaged over lags -max_lag..max_lag ms (claims, fig3e). Units whose rate on a trial is
    at or below the PI's 0.05 spikes/s do not enter that trial."""
    n = len(sp_list)
    acc, cnt = np.zeros((n, n)), np.zeros((n, n))
    rates = [mnav.smoothed_rates(sp, t0, t1) for sp in sp_list]
    for k in range(len(t0)):
        X = np.array([mnav._detrend(r[k]) for r in rates])
        ok = np.array([r[k].mean() > mnav.MIN_TRIAL_RATE for r in rates]) & (np.linalg.norm(X, axis=1) > 0)
        Xn = np.where(ok[:, None], X / np.where(ok, np.linalg.norm(X, axis=1), 1)[:, None], 0)
        T = X.shape[1]
        c = sum(Xn[:, :T - l] @ Xn[:, l:].T + (Xn[:, l:] @ Xn[:, :T - l].T if l else 0) for l in range(max_lag + 1))
        c = c / (2 * max_lag + 1)
        both = np.outer(ok, ok)
        acc += np.where(both, c, 0)
        cnt += both
    iu = np.triu_indices(n, 1)
    return np.where(cnt[iu] > 0, acc[iu] / np.maximum(cnt[iu], 1), np.nan)

per_unit_score = base[base[main_col]].groupby(["monkey", "session", "unit"]).score_methods.max().reset_index()
n_per_session = per_unit_score.groupby(["monkey", "session"]).size()
print("Periodic units per session (main reading):", n_per_session.to_dict())
chrono = {"A": sorted(s["session"] for s in sessions if s["monkey"] == "A")[4],
          "M": sorted(s["session"] for s in sessions if s["monkey"] == "M")[0]}
chosen = sorted(set([(m, ss) for m, ss in chrono.items()] + [k for k, v in n_per_session.items() if v >= 20]))
print("Sessions: chronological fifth (A) and first (M) in the dandiset:", chrono, "; all with at least 20 periodic units:",
      [k for k, v in n_per_session.items() if v >= 20])
N_LAGS_BONF = {"10 ms steps": 181, "1 ms steps": 1801}
rows = []
t = time.time()
for m, ses in chosen:
    s = sess_by[ses]
    tr = s["trials"]
    mn = tr[(tr.trial_type == 3) & (tr.attempt == 1) & (tr.distance > 3) & (tr.seqq < 3) & (tr.tp.abs() < 99)]
    er = tr[(tr.trial_type == 3) & (tr.attempt == 2) & (tr.distance > 3) & (tr.seqq < 3) & (tr.tp.abs() > 1) & (tr.tp.abs() < mnav.MAX_TP_S)]
    epochs = {"MNAV": (mn.joy1onttl.values, mn.joy1offttl.values - 0.5),
              "MNAV direction 1": (mn[mn.direction == 1].joy1onttl.values, mn[mn.direction == 1].joy1offttl.values - 0.5),
              "MNAV direction -1": (mn[mn.direction == -1].joy1onttl.values, mn[mn.direction == -1].joy1offttl.values - 0.5),
              "inference": (mn.stim1onttl.values - 0.2, mn.stim1onttl.values + 1.2),
              "error": (er.joy1onttl.values, er.joy1offttl.values - 0.5)}
    cand = per_unit_score[(per_unit_score.monkey == m) & (per_unit_score.session == ses)].sort_values("score_methods", ascending=False)
    for n_units in (20, 25):
        if len(cand) < n_units:
            rows.append({"monkey": m, "session": ses, "neurons": n_units, "note": f"only {len(cand)} periodic units"})
            continue
        units = cand.unit.values[:n_units]
        xc = {name: pair_xcorr([s["spikes"][u] for u in units], a, b) for name, (a, b) in epochs.items()}
        for ref, other in (("MNAV", "inference"), ("MNAV", "error"), ("MNAV direction 1", "MNAV direction -1")):
            ok = np.isfinite(xc[ref]) & np.isfinite(xc[other])
            r_, p_ = stats.pearsonr(xc[ref][ok], xc[other][ok])
            rows.append({"monkey": m, "session": ses, "neurons": n_units, "comparison": f"{ref} vs {other}",
                         "trials": f"{len(epochs[ref][0])} / {len(epochs[other][0])}", "pairs": int(ok.sum()),
                         "r": round(r_, 3), "p": p_, **{f"p_bonferroni_{k}": min(1.0, p_ * v) for k, v in N_LAGS_BONF.items()},
                         "meets(r>0, p_bonf<0.05)": bool(r_ > 0 and p_ * N_LAGS_BONF["1 ms steps"] < 0.05)})
ed5 = pd.DataFrame(rows)

fig4h-periodic-fano-factor¶

Many EC neurons have a Fano factor that is periodic at about 0.65 s: 55% (341/614) in monkey A and 43% (378/864) in monkey M.

Extended Data Fig. 8 legend and claims (from the code): correct MNAV trials with |tp| >= 2.3 s (seqq < 3), per direction, at least 12 trials; spike counts in 200 ms windows stepped by 30 ms from joystick onset. The end of the time course is not given; it is taken here as 500 ms before the shortest trial's offset, as for the PI (an assumption). Fano factor across trials, bootstrapped 100 times (trials resampled); Poisson null from the unit's mean count time course, 100 times; each Fano time course linearly detrended, autocorrelated to 1.6 s, and its PI computed as for the rate, in 30 ms steps (650 ms is read at the nearest step, 660 ms). Selection readings: (a) legend, maximum PI in the 300 to 900 ms lag window above the null by a two-sample t-test at p < 0.0001/20; (b) code, PI at 650 ms against the null by a one-tailed Welch t-test at 0.01. Direction readings: (i) either direction, (ii) direction 1. Periodicity: lag of the maximum mean bootstrap PI over 100 to 1,600 ms. Counts are compared as proportions of the units the dandiset holds, as for fig2.

rng4h = np.random.default_rng(48)
STEP, WIN = 0.03, 0.2
max_lag = int(round(1.6 / STEP))
flags = np.arange(0, max_lag + 1)
i660 = int(round(0.65 / STEP))
win_lo, win_hi = int(np.ceil(0.3 / STEP)), int(np.floor(0.9 / STEP))

def series_pi(x):
    """PI curve (lags 0..1.6 s in 30 ms steps) of a time course, detrended, ACG normalised at 0."""
    t_ = np.arange(len(x))
    d = x - np.polyval(np.polyfit(t_, x, 1), t_)
    n = len(d)
    nfft = 1 << int(np.ceil(np.log2(2 * n + 2 * max_lag + 2)))
    F = np.fft.rfft(d, nfft)
    ac = np.fft.irfft(F * np.conj(F), nfft)
    if ac[0] <= 0:
        return None
    ac = ac[:max_lag + 1] / ac[0]
    full = np.concatenate([ac[:0:-1], ac])
    return mnav.pi_curve(full, flags)

def fano_curves(counts, rng, n=100, poisson=False):
    out = []
    mu = counts.mean(0)
    for _ in range(n):
        c = rng.poisson(np.broadcast_to(mu, counts.shape)) if poisson else counts[rng.integers(0, len(counts), len(counts))]
        m_, v_ = c.mean(0), c.var(0, ddof=1)
        ff = np.where(m_ > 0, v_ / np.where(m_ > 0, m_, 1), 0.0)
        p = series_pi(ff)
        if p is not None:
            out.append(p)
    return np.array(out)

rows = []
for s in sessions:
    tr = s["trials"]
    for d in (1, -1):
        g = tr[(tr.trial_type == 3) & (tr.attempt == 1) & (tr.tp.abs() >= 2.3) & (tr.tp.abs() < 99) & (tr.seqq < 3) & (tr.direction == d)]
        if len(g) < 12:
            continue
        on = g.joy1onttl.values
        end = g.tp.abs().min() - mnav.OFFSET_CUT_S
        starts = np.arange(0, end - WIN + 1e-9, STEP)
        for u, sp in enumerate(s["spikes"]):
            counts = np.stack([np.searchsorted(sp, on + a + WIN) - np.searchsorted(sp, on + a) for a in starts], axis=1)
            if counts.sum() == 0:
                continue
            boot = fano_curves(counts, rng4h)
            null = fano_curves(counts, rng4h, poisson=True)
            if len(boot) < 10 or len(null) < 10:
                continue
            bmax = boot[:, win_lo:win_hi + 1].max(1)
            nmax = null[:, win_lo:win_hi + 1].max(1)
            ta_ = stats.ttest_ind(bmax, nmax)
            tb_ = stats.ttest_ind(boot[:, i660], null[:, i660], equal_var=False, alternative="greater")
            mean_pi = boot.mean(0)

            rows.append({"monkey": s["monkey"], "session": s["session"], "unit": u, "direction": d, "trials": len(g),
                         "sel_a": bool(ta_.pvalue < 1e-4 / 20 and bmax.mean() > nmax.mean()),
                         "sel_b": bool(tb_.pvalue < 0.01),
                         "fano_period": (lo + int(np.argmax(mean_pi[lo:]))) * STEP})

ed8-fano-periodic-without-rate-periodicity¶

The periodic Fano factor is not a by-product of firing-rate periodicity; it is also present in neurons whose firing rate is not periodic.

Units not periodic in rate (each periodic set, either direction) that have a periodic Fano factor (fig4h readings). One-sided binomial test of their count against 5% of all units (main) and, as variants, 5% of the non-periodic units and the false-positive rate of the Fano selection itself, measured on simulated Poisson units with each sampled unit's own mean count time course.

Among units not periodic in rate under the main reading, 193 of 308 (A) and 334 of 672 (M) have a periodic Fano factor under the legend's selection and either direction, far above 5% of all units (binomial p 1.0e-147 and 3.1e-227). The measured false-positive rate of that selection is 3.3% (A) and 2.0% (M) per unit-direction (6.6% and 4.0% per unit over two directions), and the counts are far above it too (p 2.0e-145 and 3.1e-274). The code's selection has false-positive rates of 22.0% and 16.7% per unit-direction; its counts are still above them (p 1.4e-06 or below). Every selection, direction and periodic-set reading gives p < 1e-12 against 5% of all units (largest 4.0e-13, rule b, monkey A). The counts are larger than the code's unlabelled 99/614 and 74/864, as the Fano selection here admits more units (fig4h).

fig2e-first-peak-near-065 and fig2f-earlier-peaks-multiples: phase of the local peaks¶

Methods (Quantification of the phase of local bumps) and claims (from the code): per periodic unit and direction in which it is periodic, for each periodic set; first-attempt trials not flagged as lapses (validtrials_mm), distance 4 or 5, seqq < 3; trials with no spikes from 1.5 to 0.5 s before offset dropped (the claims give "low rate" without a threshold; the PI's 0.05 spikes/s is used, an assumption); at least 25 trials. 100 times, the smoothed rate averaged over a random third of the trials; the first peak is the highest local maximum (findpeaks, prominence 0.05 on the min-max normalised window) in the 1 s before offset (Methods), the second in the 1 s before the first, the third in the 1 s before the second. Null: each trial's spike train circularly shifted by a random length within the 3.5 s analysed, then the same. Per unit, the KS test of bootstrap against null first-peak phases, the mode of the bootstrap phases (10 ms bins, a standard choice) and the median intervals between peaks. Across units whose KS p < 0.001, the median of the modes; readings for the KS P << 0.0001: (a) per unit, (b) pooled phases. Variant: the code's -1 to -0.1 s window, on the main reading's units.

from scipy.signal import find_peaks

rng2e = np.random.default_rng(265)
SPAN = 3.5

def peak_phases(rate, first_window=(-1.0, 0.0)):
    """Phases (s, negative) of the first three peaks of a rate on the window [-SPAN, 0) before offset."""
    out = []
    hi = first_window[1]
    lo = first_window[0]
    for _ in range(3):
        a, b = int(round((SPAN + lo) * 1000)), int(round((SPAN + hi) * 1000))
        if a < 0 or b - a < 3:
            out.append(np.nan)
            continue
        seg = rate[a:b]
        rngv = seg.max() - seg.min()
        if rngv <= 0:
            out.append(np.nan)
            continue
        x = (seg - seg.min()) / rngv
        pk, _ = find_peaks(x, prominence=0.05)
        if len(pk) == 0:
            out.append(np.nan)
            break
        best = pk[np.argmax(x[pk])]
        phase = (a + best) / 1000 - SPAN
        out.append(phase)
        hi, lo = phase, phase - 1.0
    while len(out) < 3:
        out.append(np.nan)
    return out

def phase_unit(counts, rng, n=100, window=(-1.0, 0.0)):
    k = max(1, len(counts) // 3)
    boot, null = [], []
    for _ in range(n):
        idx = rng.choice(len(counts), k, replace=False)
        r = gaussian(counts[idx].mean(0))
        boot.append(peak_phases(r, window))
        sh = np.stack([np.roll(counts[i], int(rng.integers(0, counts.shape[1]))) for i in idx])
        null.append(peak_phases(gaussian(sh.mean(0)), window))
    return np.array(boot), np.array(null)

from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d
def gaussian(x):
    return gaussian_filter1d(x, mnav.SMOOTH_SD_MS, truncate=mnav.SMOOTH_TRUNCATE, mode="nearest") * 1000

set_cols = list(dict.fromkeys(SETS.values()))
periodic_pairs = base[base[set_cols].any(axis=1)][["monkey", "session", "unit", "direction"] + set_cols]
sess_by = {s["session"]: s for s in sessions}
t = time.time()
rows, pooled = [], {}
for window_name, window in (("methods_-1_0", (-1.0, 0.0)), ("code_-1_-0.1", (-1.0, -0.1))):
    # the code's window is run on the main reading's units only
    pairs = periodic_pairs if window_name == "methods_-1_0" else periodic_pairs[periodic_pairs[main_col]]
    for r in pairs.itertuples():
        s = sess_by[r.session]
        tr = s["trials"]
        g = tr[(tr.trial_type == 3) & (tr.attempt == 1) & (tr.validtrials_mm == 1) & tr.distance.isin([4, 5])
               & (tr.seqq < 3) & (tr.direction == r.direction)]
        sp = s["spikes"][r.unit]
        off = g.joy1offttl.values
        keep = mnav.mean_rate(sp, off - 1.5, off - 0.5) > mnav.MIN_TRIAL_RATE
        off = off[keep]
        if len(off) < 25:
            rows.append({"window": window_name, "monkey": r.monkey, "session": r.session, "unit": r.unit, "direction": r.direction, "trials": len(off)})
            continue
        counts, _n = mnav.trial_counts(sp, off - SPAN, off)
        boot, null = phase_unit(counts, rng2e, window=window)
        b1, n1 = boot[:, 0][np.isfinite(boot[:, 0])], null[:, 0][np.isfinite(null[:, 0])]
        ks = stats.ks_2samp(b1, n1).pvalue if len(b1) > 1 and len(n1) > 1 else np.nan
        row = {"window": window_name, "monkey": r.monkey, "session": r.session, "unit": r.unit, "direction": r.direction,
               "trials": len(off), "ks_p": ks}
        for j, name in enumerate(("first", "second", "third")):
            v = boot[:, j][np.isfinite(boot[:, j])]
            if len(v):
                h, e = np.histogram(v, bins=np.arange(-SPAN, 0.0001, 0.01))
                row[f"mode_{name}"] = round(e[h.argmax()] + 0.005, 3)
        pooled[(window_name, r.monkey, r.session, r.unit, r.direction)] = (b1, n1)
        row["interval_1_2"] = float(np.nanmedian(boot[:, 0] - boot[:, 1])) if np.isfinite(boot[:, 1]).any() else np.nan
        row["interval_2_3"] = float(np.nanmedian(boot[:, 1] - boot[:, 2])) if np.isfinite(boot[:, 2]).any() else np.nan
        rows.append(row)
phase = pd.DataFrame(rows).merge(periodic_pairs, on=["monkey", "session", "unit", "direction"])
print(f"phase analysis in {time.time() - t:.0f} s; periodic unit-directions: {len(periodic_pairs)}; "

def peak_set_rows(variant_rows, exclude=()):
    rows = []
    for set_name, set_col in SETS.items():
        for (w, m), g in phase[phase.ks_p.notna() & phase[set_col] & ~phase.session.isin(exclude)].groupby(["window", "monkey"]):
            if w != "methods_-1_0" and set_col != main_col:     # the code's window is run on the main reading only
                continue
            sig = g[g.ks_p < 0.001]
            keys = [(w, r.monkey, r.session, r.unit, r.direction) for r in g.itertuples()]
            b = np.concatenate([pooled[k][0] for k in keys])
            nn = np.concatenate([pooled[k][1] for k in keys])
            rows.append({"periodic_set": set_name, "window": w, "monkey": m, "units_tested": len(g), "units_ks_p<0.001": len(sig),
                         "units_ks_p<0.0001": int((g.ks_p < 1e-4).sum()), "frac_p<0.0001": round(float((g.ks_p < 1e-4).mean()), 3),
                         "pooled_ks_p": stats.ks_2samp(b, nn).pvalue, **variant_rows(sig)})
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

    return {"median_first_mode_s": sig.mode_first.median(),
            "first_mode_iqr": f"{sig.mode_first.quantile(.25):.2f}..{sig.mode_first.quantile(.75):.2f}",
            "in_-0.70_-0.60": bool(-0.70 <= sig.mode_first.median() <= -0.60)}

Result: not reproduced. Under the main reading and the Methods' window, the median second-peak mode is -1.245 s in monkey A and -1.070 s in monkey M, against -1.30 s, and the third -1.445 and -1.745 s, against -1.95 s. The median interval between the first and second peak within a unit is 0.550 s (A) and 0.344 s (M), and between the second and third 0.407 and 0.394 s, shorter than 0.65 s. Monkey A's second peak is within 0.05 s of -1.30 s under the code's window (-1.255 s, 45 units), rule a1 (-1.310 s, 12 units) and the GP-null reading (-1.285 s, 28 units), and 0.005 s outside it under the main reading; monkey M's second peak is outside it under every reading, and no reading puts the third peak near -1.95 s in either monkey. So the second peak holds at most in one monkey and the third in neither, which meets neither partial clause cleanly. Leaving out A 09172019 gives -1.240 s for A's second peak. Pooled over both monkeys the medians are -1.205 and -1.495 s.

ed3-no-eye-hand-periodicity¶

Eye position (horizontal and vertical) and joystick position during the navigation epoch show no periodicity; their PI at 650 ms is below chance.

In five monkey A sessions the eye and joystick timestamps span the trial times. In the other ten (A 08152019 and every monkey M session) they are on another clock, whose offset the files do not give; it is estimated here by cross-correlating the time the joystick is deflected with the intervals between the trial table's joystick onsets and offsets (mnav.behaviour_clock_offset). The same estimate in the five sessions on the trial clock gives -0.12 to -0.26 s, so its median (-0.17 s) is taken as the estimate's bias and subtracted. Each shifted session is kept only if, after the shift, the joystick deviates from rest at least twice as much 0.2 to 0.45 s after the recorded onsets as before them, and more than 7 s later. The signals are treated as the rates are for the PI (claims): PI trials of both directions pooled, joystick onset to 500 ms before offset, the trace interpolated to 1 ms and smoothed with the rate kernel, each trial detrended, mean ACG, PI (Methods lags). Bootstrap readings: (a) 100 resamples of the pooled trials with replacement, full size; (b) 100 subsamples of a third without replacement. Null: Gaussian process surrogates (SE kernel, length 100 ms) smoothed as the signals, without the Poisson step (the signals are continuous), averaged over as many trials as a bootstrap sample, 1,000 times. Chance readings: (a) the surrogate PI at 650 ms mean + 2 SD; (b) its mean. One-tailed one-sample t-test of the 100 bootstrap PIs at 650 ms against chance, per monkey.

from scipy.ndimage import gaussian_filter1d as _g1d
rng3 = np.random.default_rng(3003)
# Each session's eye and joystick traces. Where their timestamps do not span the trial times (A
# 08152019 and the monkey M sessions), the clock offset is estimated from the joystick trace
# (mnav.behaviour_clock_offset) and the traces are shifted by it; the estimate is also made, as a
# check, in the sessions whose traces are on the trial clock, where it should be near 0.
signals = {}
rows, ests = [], []
t = time.time()
# the sessions on the trial clock come first, so that the median of their estimates (the bias of
# the estimate) can be subtracted from the others
def _on_clock(s):
    return (abs(s["info"]["eye_ts_first"] - s["trials"].start_time.min()) < 500
            and abs(s["info"]["eye_ts_last"] - s["trials"].stop_time.max()) < 500)
calib = 0.0
for s in sorted(sessions, key=lambda s: not _on_clock(s)):
    if not _on_clock(s) and ests and calib == 0.0:
        calib = float(np.median([e for c, e in ests if c]))
        print(f"median estimate in the sessions on the trial clock (bias subtracted from the others): {calib:.3f} s")
    asset = [a for a in mnav.assets() if a.path == s["path"]][0]
    f = mnav._open(asset)
    on_clock = _on_clock(s)
    hts = f["processing/behavior/hand_position/timestamps"][:]
    hx = f["processing/behavior/hand_position/data"][:].ravel()
    est, z, second = mnav.behaviour_clock_offset(hts, hx, s["trials"])
    ests.append((on_clock, est))
    shift = 0.0 if on_clock else est - calib
    tr = mnav.pi_trials(s["trials"])
    t0, t1 = mnav.nav_windows(tr)
    ets = f["processing/behavior/eye_position/timestamps"][:] - shift
    elo, ehi = np.searchsorted(ets, t0 - 0.01), np.searchsorted(ets, t1 + 0.01)
    e0 = int(elo.min()) if len(elo) else 0
    eye = f["processing/behavior/eye_position/data"][e0:int(ehi.max()) if len(ehi) else 0]     # one read
    for name, col in (("eye_x", 0), ("eye_y", 1), ("joystick", None)):
        ts = hts - shift if col is None else ets
        lo, hi = (np.searchsorted(ts, t0 - 0.01), np.searchsorted(ts, t1 + 0.01)) if col is None else (elo, ehi)
        for a, b, x0, x1 in zip(lo, hi, t0, t1):
            if b - a < 10:
                continue
            seg = hx[a:b] if col is None else eye[a - e0:b - e0, col]
            signals.setdefault((s["monkey"], s["session"], name), []).append(np.interp(np.arange(x0, x1, 0.001), ts[a:b], seg))
    # clock check: joystick deflection around the trial table's joystick onsets, after the shift
    hts_s = hts - shift
    on = s["trials"][(s["trials"].trial_type == 3) & (s["trials"].attempt == 1)].joy1onttl.values[:200]
    pre = np.concatenate([hx[x:y] for x, y in zip(np.searchsorted(hts_s, on - 0.3), np.searchsorted(hts_s, on - 0.05))])
    rest = float(np.median(pre)) if len(pre) else np.nan
    def dev(times, a_, b_):
        l_, h_ = np.searchsorted(hts_s, times + a_), np.searchsorted(hts_s, times + b_)
        v = [np.abs(hx[x:y] - rest).mean() for x, y in zip(l_, h_) if y > x]
        return float(np.mean(v)) if v else np.nan
    rows.append({"monkey": s["monkey"], "session": s["session"], "on_trial_clock": on_clock,
                 "estimated_offset_s": round(est, 3), "peak_z": round(z, 1), "far_peak/peak": round(second, 3),
                 "shift_used_s": round(shift, 3), "PI_trials": len(tr), "traces": len(signals.get((s["monkey"], s["session"], "joystick"), [])),
                 "|dev| before onset (V)": round(dev(on, -0.3, -0.05), 3), "|dev| 0.2-0.45 s after onset": round(dev(on, 0.2, 0.45), 3),
                 "same, onset + 7 s": round(dev(on + 7.0, 0.2, 0.45), 3)})
beh = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(f"streamed in {time.time() - t:.0f} s")
print(beh.to_string(index=False))

def smooth_trace(x):
    return _g1d(x, mnav.SMOOTH_SD_MS, truncate=mnav.SMOOTH_TRUNCATE, mode="nearest")

def acgs_of(traces):
    out = []
    for x in traces:
        a, _k = mnav.mean_acg([smooth_trace(x)], min_rate=-np.inf)
        if a is not None:
            out.append(a)
    return np.array(out)

def gp_trace(rng, n):
    sig = mnav.GP_LENGTH_MS / np.sqrt(2)
    w = rng.standard_normal(n + 800)
    return _g1d(w, sig, mode="wrap")[400:400 + n]

lags = mnav.LAGS_METHODS
i650 = int(np.nonzero(lags == 650)[0][0])
clock_ok = beh[(beh.on_trial_clock) | ((beh["|dev| 0.2-0.45 s after onset"] > 2 * beh["|dev| before onset (V)"])
                                     & (beh["|dev| 0.2-0.45 s after onset"] > beh["same, onset + 7 s"]))]
rows = []
for m in ("A", "M"):
    ses_m = clock_ok[clock_ok.monkey == m].session.tolist()
    durations = [len(x) for ss in ses_m for x in signals.get((m, ss, "joystick"), [])]
    if not durations:
        continue
    bank = acgs_of([gp_trace(rng3, n) for n in rng3.choice(durations, 3000)])
    for name in ("eye_x", "eye_y", "joystick"):
        A_ = acgs_of([x for ss in ses_m for x in signals.get((m, ss, name), [])])
        n = len(A_)
        for boot in ("a_full_with_replacement", "b_third_without"):
            k = n if boot.startswith("a") else n // 3
            w = np.zeros((100, n))
            for j in range(100):
                idx = rng3.integers(0, n, n) if boot.startswith("a") else rng3.choice(n, k, replace=False)
                np.add.at(w[j], idx, 1.0 / k)
            bpi = mnav.pi_curves(w @ A_, {"m": lags})["m"][:, i650]
            wn = np.zeros((1000, len(bank)))
            for j in range(1000):
                np.add.at(wn[j], rng3.integers(0, len(bank), k), 1.0 / k)
            null = mnav.pi_curves(wn @ bank, {"m": lags})["m"][:, i650]
            for chance_name, chance in (("a_mean+2SD", null.mean() + 2 * null.std()), ("b_mean", null.mean())):
                lo_ = stats.ttest_1samp(bpi, chance, alternative="less")
                hi_ = stats.ttest_1samp(bpi, chance, alternative="greater")
                rows.append({"monkey": m, "sessions": len(ses_m), "signal": name, "trials": n, "bootstrap": boot, "chance": chance_name,
                             "mean_PI650": round(bpi.mean(), 3), "chance_value": round(chance, 3), "t(99)": round(lo_.statistic, 1),

                             "below_p<1e-4": bool(lo_.pvalue < 1e-4), "above_p<0.05": bool(hi_.pvalue < 0.05)})

Result: reproduced. In both monkeys the PI at 650 ms is below chance for all three signals under every bootstrap and chance reading (one-tailed t-test, p 5.7e-52 to 1.2e-183), and no signal is above chance (one-tailed p = 1.0). Monkey A (6 sessions, 2,088 trials): mean PI 0.155 (horizontal eye), 0.117 (vertical eye) and -0.401 (joystick), against chance values of 0.230 to 0.303. Monkey M (9 sessions, 1,998 trials): -0.370, -0.159 and -0.452, against 0.310 to 0.384. The mean PIs differ from the paper's -0.25, -0.44 and -0.53, by more than the 10% tolerance in every case, and the eye PIs of monkey A are positive. The clock offset of ten sessions is estimated, not given by the files: after the shift the joystick deviates from rest by 2.39 to 2.53 V after the recorded onsets, against 0.16 to 0.84 V before them and 0.73 to 1.39 V 7 s later, the pattern of the five sessions on the trial clock (0.43 to 0.70 V, 1.95 to 2.49 V and 1.08 to 1.32 V).

fig4g-reset-model-fits-better¶

A Bayesian observer model whose timing variability grows sublinearly, as with resets at multiples of 0.65 s, fits the monkeys' behaviour better than a scalar-variability model without resets.

Criterion (claims): per session, both observer models of the code's utilities (models 1 and 2: Bayes least squares estimate of a noisy measurement under the code's prior, density 0.5846 - 0.1026 t on 0.65 to 3.25 s; measurement and production noise SD wm t and wp t_e without resets, wm sqrt(t) and wp sqrt(t_e) with resets, as in utilities/bls_offset_*_nonuniformPrior_self.m; offset b) fit by maximum likelihood (Nelder-Mead from [0.5, 0.5, 0], as fminsearch) to |v_p| against |v_a| of correct MNAV trials (seqq < 3, as the prior covers 0.65 to 3.25 s). Lapses excluded first by a Gaussian and uniform mixture per interval (Methods; the uniform's range "0 to 3 v_p" is read as 0 to 3 times the interval, an assumption); without exclusion (code) as a variant. Model error per session: the absolute difference between the data's and the model's summed squared bias plus variance across the five intervals (code line 118). Paired t-test of no-reset against reset error across sessions, all sessions and, as the code does, without the first; the code's two-sample test (line 1133) as a variant. The dandiset holds 6 and 9 sessions, where the paper's degrees of freedom imply 79 and 103.
