t = time.time()
rows = []
for s in sessions:
    tr = s["trials"]
    g = tr[(tr.trial_type == 3) & (tr.attempt == 1) & (tr.seqq < 3) & (tr.tp.abs() > 0.01) & (tr.tp.abs() < 99)]
    ta, tp = np.round(g.ta.abs().values, 3), g.tp.abs().values
    for lapse in ("Methods: lapses excluded", "code: no exclusion"):
        keep = mnav.lapse_mask(ta, tp) if lapse.startswith("Methods") else np.ones(len(tp), bool)
        a, p = ta[keep], tp[keep]
        ts = np.unique(a)
        data_bias = np.array([p[a == x].mean() - x for x in ts])
        data_var = np.array([p[a == x].var() for x in ts])
        row = {"monkey": s["monkey"], "session": s["session"], "lapses": lapse, "trials": int(keep.sum()), "dropped": int((~keep).sum())}
        for model, reset in (("no_reset", False), ("reset", True)):
            fit = mnav.bls_fit(a, p, reset)
            mb, mv = mnav.bls_bias_var(fit.x, ts, reset)
            row[f"{model}_wm"], row[f"{model}_wp"], row[f"{model}_b"] = np.round([abs(fit.x[0]), abs(fit.x[1]), fit.x[2]], 3)
            row[f"{model}_nll"] = round(fit.fun, 1)
            row[f"{model}_converged"] = bool(fit.success)
            row[f"{model}_error"] = abs(np.sum(data_bias ** 2 + data_var) - np.sum(mb ** 2 + mv))
        rows.append(row)
fig4g = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(f"fits in {time.time() - t:.0f} s")
print(fig4g.round(4).to_string(index=False))
res = []
for (lapse, m), g in fig4g.groupby(["lapses", "monkey"]):
    for test_name, sub in (("paired, all sessions", g), ("paired, first session left out (code)", g.sort_values("session").iloc[1:])):
        tt = stats.ttest_rel(sub.no_reset_error, sub.reset_error)
        res.append({"lapses": lapse, "monkey": m, "test": test_name, "sessions": len(sub),
                    "mean_error_no_reset": round(sub.no_reset_error.mean(), 4), "mean_error_reset": round(sub.reset_error.mean(), 4),
                    "reset_lower_in": f"{int((sub.reset_error < sub.no_reset_error).sum())}/{len(sub)}",
                    "t": round(tt.statistic, 2), "df": len(sub) - 1, "p_two_sided": tt.pvalue,
                    "meets(reset lower, p<1e-4)": bool(tt.statistic > 0 and tt.pvalue < 1e-4)})
    tt2 = stats.ttest_ind(g.no_reset_error, g.reset_error)
    res.append({"lapses": lapse, "monkey": m, "test": "two-sample (code line 1133)", "sessions": len(g), "t": round(tt2.statistic, 2),
                "df": 2 * len(g) - 2, "p_two_sided": tt2.pvalue, "meets(reset lower, p<1e-4)": bool(tt2.statistic > 0 and tt2.pvalue < 1e-4)})
print(pd.DataFrame(res).to_string(index=False))
print("Log-likelihood difference (no reset minus reset NLL; positive favours reset), per monkey, median:",
      (fig4g.no_reset_nll - fig4g.reset_nll).groupby([fig4g.lapses, fig4g.monkey]).median().round(1).to_dict())

# Effect size of the paired test (mean difference over its SD, d_z = t / sqrt(n)), beside the paper's
# from its t and degrees of freedom (claims file: A t(77) = 7.93, M t(101) = 16.56), and the t that a
# two-sided p < 0.0001 needs with the sessions held here.
paper_t = {"A": (7.93, 77), "M": (16.56, 101)}
for m, g in fig4g[fig4g.lapses == "Methods: lapses excluded"].groupby("monkey"):
    d = g.no_reset_error - g.reset_error
    t_need = stats.t.isf(0.5e-4, len(d) - 1)
    print(f"monkey {m}: d_z = {d.mean() / d.std(ddof=1):.2f} over {len(d)} sessions; paper d_z = "
          f"{paper_t[m][0] / np.sqrt(paper_t[m][1] + 1):.2f} over {paper_t[m][1] + 1}; "
          f"t needed for p < 0.0001 with {len(d)} sessions {t_need:.1f}")

Result: partially reproduced. The model with resets has the lower error in all 15 sessions (mean error 0.0188 against 0.1488 in A, 0.0247 against 0.1359 in M) and the higher likelihood in 14 (median log-likelihood difference 51.6 in A and 7.8 in M). The paired t-test across sessions does not reach p < 0.0001 in either monkey (A t(5) = 9.26, p = 2.5e-04; M t(8) = 4.99, p = 1.1e-03, two-sided), nor without the first session as the code does (p 1.2e-03 and 3.4e-03). The code's two-sample test gives p < 0.0001 in both (about 2e-06 and 1.3e-05). The mixture model excluded no trial (the trials are first-attempt trials), so the Methods' and the code's fits are the same. The dandiset holds 6 and 9 sessions, where the paper's degrees of freedom imply 79 and 103 (78 and 102 pairs in its test). The paired effect size is as large as the paper's or larger (d_z printed above), and the t that p < 0.0001 needs with 6 and 9 sessions is above the observed t. The criterion defines only the reproduced outcome. The effect is present and in the paper's direction in every session, and its test is weaker because of the number of sessions, so the outcome is partially reproduced under the protocol's definition (effect present but weaker); the verifier would give not reproduced, and that disagreement is recorded.

fig4d-model-subscalar-variability¶

The CAN model without landmarks shows scalar variability, its SD growing linearly with temporal distance, while the model with endogenous landmarks shows subscalar variability, with a power-law exponent below 1.

A simulation, not a test on recorded data. The model is ported from the paper's code (mnav.can_*, from gc_CAN_model_simulation.m and utilities/gc1d_*.m at commit 4bee109, the code the claims file cites). Weber fraction 0.08: the claims file writes 0.8 for the file Fig. 4c loads (wm8), but the code names its files with 100 times the Weber fraction, and its Fig. 4c section sets wmm = .08; a Weber fraction of 0.8 would make some velocities negative. This is asked of a reader (questions/000897.yaml). 50 simulations with landmarks at velocity 0.42 (1 + 0.08 N(0, 1)); the time to reach the network state that the median landmark trajectory has at 0.65, 1.30, ..., 3.25 s (code, get_simul_variance, steps counted as 1/20,000 s as the code does). Without landmarks the dynamics depend only on the velocity, so a grid of noise-free velocities (0.28 to 0.465) is simulated and the times of 50 noisy velocities are interpolated from it. No-landmark velocity: per base interval by grid search so that the mean time matches the landmark model's (Methods, main); the script's single 0.35 as a variant. 1,000 bootstrap SDs and means per interval; SD = a mean^b + c fitted per bootstrap (claims), and a mean^b (the code's lsqcurvefit, a variant); one-tailed t-test of b against 1.

In [32]:
from scipy.optimize import curve_fit
rng4d = np.random.default_rng(404)
t = time.time()
W_can = mnav.can_setup()
s0_can = mnav.can_init(W_can, rng4d)
WM, V_LM, V_NOLM = 0.08, 0.42, 0.35          # Weber fraction of Fig. 4c (file wm8) and the script's speeds
N_SIM = 50
v_lm = V_LM * (1 + WM * rng4d.standard_normal(N_SIM))
xi_nolm = rng4d.standard_normal(N_SIM)
v_grid = np.round(np.arange(0.28, 0.4651, 0.005), 3)      # no-landmark velocities, without noise
traj = mnav.can_run(W_can, s0_can, np.r_[v_lm, v_grid], np.r_[np.ones(N_SIM, bool), np.zeros(len(v_grid), bool)])
print(f"{N_SIM} simulations with landmarks and {len(v_grid)} without in {time.time() - t:.0f} s")
STEP_S = 1 / 20000                              # the code's conversion of steps to seconds (mnav_ec_fig4.m)
tr_lm = traj[:, :N_SIM].astype(float)
end_step = mnav.first_reach(traj[:, :N_SIM], 360)
for j in range(N_SIM):
    tr_lm[int(end_step[j]):, j] = np.nan
median_traj = np.nanmedian(tr_lm, axis=1)
base_time = 0.65 * np.arange(1, 6)
tt_ = np.arange(1, len(median_traj) + 1) * STEP_S
states = np.array([median_traj[np.argmax(tt_ > b)] for b in base_time])
rt_lm = np.stack([mnav.first_reach(traj[:, :N_SIM], s_) * STEP_S for s_ in states], axis=1)
# no-landmark times as a function of velocity, interpolated for noisy velocities
grid_rt = np.stack([mnav.first_reach(traj[:, N_SIM:], s_) * STEP_S for s_ in states], axis=1)   # grid x 5

def nolm_rt(v_base):
    v = v_base * (1 + WM * xi_nolm)
    return np.stack([np.interp(v, v_grid, grid_rt[:, i]) for i in range(5)], axis=1)

# Methods (CAN model): the no-landmark velocity set by a grid search for each base interval so that
# the mean time matches the landmark model's
v_fit = []
cand = np.arange(0.30, 0.42, 0.0005)
for i in range(5):
    err = [abs(nolm_rt(c)[:, i].mean() - rt_lm[:, i].mean()) for c in cand]
    v_fit.append(cand[int(np.argmin(err))])
rt_nolm_methods = np.stack([nolm_rt(v_fit[i])[:, i] for i in range(5)], axis=1)
rt_nolm_script = nolm_rt(V_NOLM)
print("Network state at the base intervals (median landmark trajectory):", states.astype(int).tolist())
print("No-landmark velocity per base interval (grid search):", np.round(v_fit, 4).tolist(),
      "; velocities outside the simulated grid:", int(((V_NOLM * (1 + WM * xi_nolm) < v_grid[0]) | (V_NOLM * (1 + WM * xi_nolm) > v_grid[-1])).sum()))

def power_b(rt, with_c, n_boot=1000):
    idx = rng4d.integers(0, len(rt), (n_boot, len(rt)))
    sds = np.stack([rt[idx, i].std(1, ddof=1) for i in range(5)], axis=1)
    means = np.stack([rt[idx, i].mean(1) for i in range(5)], axis=1)
    bs = []
    for j in range(n_boot):
        try:
            if with_c:
                # started from the linear fit (b = 1), a standard choice; from [0.5, 0.5, 0] the fit
                # can stop in a degenerate minimum with b near 0
                k_, c_ = np.polyfit(means[j], sds[j], 1)
                p, _ = curve_fit(lambda x, a, b, c: a * x ** b + c, means[j], sds[j], p0=[k_, 1.0, c_], maxfev=10000)
            else:
                p, _ = curve_fit(lambda x, a, b: a * x ** b, means[j], sds[j], p0=[0.5, 0.5], maxfev=10000)
            bs.append(p[1])
        except RuntimeError:
            bs.append(np.nan)
    return np.array(bs)

rows = []
for model, rt in (("landmarks", rt_lm), ("no landmarks, velocity per interval (Methods)", rt_nolm_methods),
                  ("no landmarks, velocity 0.35 (script)", rt_nolm_script)):
    for fit_name, with_c in (("a m^b + c (claims)", True), ("a m^b (code)", False)):
        bs = power_b(rt, with_c)
        ok = np.isfinite(bs)
        tt2 = stats.ttest_1samp(bs[ok], 1, alternative="less")
        rows.append({"model": model, "fit": fit_name, "mean_s": np.round(rt.mean(0), 3).tolist(), "sd_s": np.round(rt.std(0, ddof=1), 4).tolist(),
                     "cv_first_last": f"{rt[:, 0].std(ddof=1) / rt[:, 0].mean():.3f}, {rt[:, 4].std(ddof=1) / rt[:, 4].mean():.3f}",
                     "fits": int(ok.sum()), "b_mean": round(float(bs[ok].mean()), 3), "b_median": round(float(np.median(bs[ok])), 3),
                     "t(df)": f"{tt2.statistic:.2f} ({ok.sum() - 1})", "p_b<1": tt2.pvalue})
fig4d = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(fig4d.to_string(index=False))
print(f"in {time.time() - t:.0f} s")

Result: not reproduced. With the claims' fit (SD = a mean^b + c), the model with landmarks has b = 0.848 (mean of 1,000 bootstrap fits; t(999) = -1188.9, p < 1e-300), but the model without landmarks also has b below 1: 0.977 with the velocity set per base interval (t(999) = -80.0) and 0.990 at the script's 0.35 (t(999) = -611.5), both p < 1e-300, so the second condition fails. With the code's fit (SD = a mean^b) the landmark model has b = 0.977 (t(999) = -292.4) and the no-landmark model 1.009 (not below 1, p = 1.0) with the Methods' velocities, which would meet the criterion, while at 0.35 it is 1.000 (t(999) = -13.2, p = 3.4e-37). In the simulations the coefficient of variation hardly changes with the interval in either model (0.065 to 0.067 with landmarks, 0.072 to 0.074 without), so the ported model shows little of the subscalar variability of Fig. 4d. The t-test treats 1,000 bootstrap fits of the same 50 simulations as independent, so any b that differs from 1 by a few thousandths is significant. The model is a port of the paper's MATLAB code, run here for the first time; Fig. 4d's own simulations are not available to compare.

A failure to reproduce here may be a failure of this attempt, not of the paper: see the reasoning and the differences from the paper's method.

How the analysis differs from the paper's. The dandiset holds 15 of the 32 sessions, so counts are compared as proportions. The PI null turns the Gaussian process into a firing rate by exponentiation at the group's median unit rate, which the Methods do not describe; it is built from a bank of surrogate trials and matched to each unit's number of kept trials; the code's GP null without the Poisson step is run as a variant. The classification rule is open and every reading is shown; fig2d, ed2c, ed4d, ed10 and the other claims that use periodic units are run under the main reading (the code's score against the surrogate scores) and under rules a1 and b and the GP null, and their outcomes rest on the main reading. The population regression of fig3d centres each unit across both windows, as the Methods state; centring per window and time bin, as the cited method's constant term does, is run as a variant and gives offset above onset in both monkeys, where the Methods' centring gives a reversal in monkey M. Monkey M's sequence 3 trials are left out wherever distance is used, as the code does for the PI. All units are used, including those labelled noise in monkey A. The eye and joystick clock of ten sessions is an estimate made here. The Bayesian observer models and the CAN model are ported from the paper's MATLAB code to Python.

What was found about the dataset. It holds 15 of the 32 sessions, with 1,093 units (364 and 729) against the paper's 1,478; 103 monkey A units are labelled noise. Monkey M's seqq 3 trials use vectors in steps of 0.975 s, which the paper does not describe. The eye and joystick timestamps are on another clock than the trials in 10 of the 15 sessions, offset by 3,326 to 1,561,450 s by the estimate made here; the files do not give the offset. In three sessions (A 09172019, M 04132021, M 04142021) no unit's rate changes around joystick offset, and in M 04132021 the spikes stop halfway through the trials, so a shared clock could not be established. The ITI is not marked, and the ITI segments longer than 4 s the paper uses cannot be found. Rows with attempt 2 hold the first attempt's joystick times, which the files do not describe. Unit labels differ between monkeys (quality in A, only KSLabel in M), and most unit columns have no description.
